newsitem.title: UK: Costume jewellery firm Cabouchon to launch in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Costume jewellery firm Cabouchon to launch in U.S.

text.p: Cabouchon, a glitzy costume jewellery firm, launches in the United States next week, hoping to repeat its rapid growth in Europe and Japan.
Petra Doring, German-born socialite who founded the company six years ago, said on Wednesday she thought the group could be a success in the U.S. market.

Doring, 36, who started the business with 100,000 pounds ($167,300) of privately raised capital, said at first she was wary of the U.S. market. "Initially, to be honest, I was a little bit scared because the U.S. has so much costume jewellery, but when we started our trials we had fantastic success," she said by telephone.
The company, with sales of about 120 million pounds ($200.8 million) last year, operates via a network of "consultants", individuals who sell directly to friends or run teams of other sellers.
It now operates in 17 countries and currently has 16,000 "consultants" -- including some celebrities and aristocrats -- who earn commission on what they sell.
The jewellery, which costs between four and 140 pounds, is shipped to customers in Europe from a warehouse in Britain, which will begin servicing the U.S.. It also has a warehouse in Japan.

The company launches two new jewellery ranges each year, and takes a theme for each one such as the Russian Tsars or images of India. But has also recently expanded into accessories such as belts, buckles, watches and ties. ($1=.5976 Pound)
